coverage:
Read-only pass over node-1 SurrealDB activity-system/learning_loop, run 2026-09-29 04:00–04:40 UTC.
- Server level: listed namespaces and got a row count for every one of the 100 tables.
- Migration ledger (init_migrations) diffed against activity-api, concept-db and identity-vessel sql/ in the host repo, the container /vessels tree and the push clone.
- concept table: shape and source_type cardinality, recency, load counters, embedding coverage, org split.
- All 45 compose_lesson rows read, plus their read/write code paths in feature-compose.ts.
- 719 architecturePrinciple rows.
- 1,991 doc-derived concepts checked against the current docs tree.
- concept_edge: types, recency, traversal, dangling count (with a positive control).
- concept_usage retention.
- Oracle and outcome tables: goal_verification_labels, decision_outcome, refusal_events, promote_gate_evaluations.
- impulse table: 107,865 rows across 6 shapes.
- Other learning tables.
- concept-db /health telemetry and the hub's concept-db and dev-vessel logs (last 6h).
- Node 2 checked for concept-db/surrealdb presence, the dev-vessel's process environment, and 6h of logs.

Not done:
- No live /concepts/search calls, because each search writes concept_usage and bumps times_loaded.
- The dense-empty root cause is PLAUSIBLE only. Probing KNN with a stored vector returns neighbours of the same type, so it can't discriminate for free-text queries.
- Node 2 has no DB, so it had no DB queries.
- Content of execution_trace_content, thompson_selection_log and context_thompson_scores was not analysed; only counts. The round-1 live shards cover them.
- The compose_lesson rows carry no edit_site at all (pointer:{}), so the edit_site-existence check does not apply to them. It applies to gaps.

principles: Reads and writes of one shape must share one address: route concept writes via discovery exactly as reads are routed. A hardcoded local write endpoint silently drops every signal on a spoke.
A lesson channel that is never graded cannot learn which lessons help. Verify that the write-back route exists (a positive control) before calling the channel live.
Filter before KNN, or partition the corpus. Post-filtering a top-32 over a table that is 87% signatures starves small curated corpora.
Diagnose the zero-hit before removing a filter: the 08-09 removal was based on a false premise (719 rows existed).
Doc-derived knowledge needs a retirement field kept in sync with the docs tree. Without it, 25% of 'principles' describe text that no longer exists.
Never let two migrations share a number or redefine the same field. Lexical order silently decides the schema, and an unledgered applier re-runs both on every boot.
A UNIQUE ledger index must be proven to enforce (a positive control). Ghost ledger names mean a fresh boot diverges from live.
A shadow emitter with no reader and no retention is pure growth. Every write-only shape needs a named reader or a TTL.
A repair tool that recomputes from a table must be re-validated when that table gets a retention policy.
A gate that promotes 99.7% at the minimum sample size, re-evaluating the same templates hundreds of times, is not a gate.
Test and bisect work must use a scratch server, not scratch namespaces on the live one, and fixture goals must not be labelled into the live oracle corpus.

claims.later: False premise: 74 rows existed in June and 524 in July (719 now), and concept.ts:329 wires shape into SQL. The zero-hit was the @@-AND long-query miss. The consult now runs unfiltered over 88k rows.

claims.claim: A real query matched nothing because @@ is AND; fixed with a relaxing ladder

claims.claim: A scalar filter beside <|K,EF|> defeats HNSW; moved filters to a hydrate stage
claims.later: HNSW works (positive control), but post-filtering a top-32 plausibly empties small corpora
